# YAML: opentide-schema against the oracle

<!-- Generated by crates/opentide-schema/tests/yaml_table.rs from tests/oracle/yaml_cases.toml and tests/oracle/yaml_table.json. Do not edit: UPDATE_YAML_TABLE=1 cargo test -p opentide-schema --test yaml_table -->

opentide-schema reads an object file as **YAML 1.2** (the core schema) with saphyr (`src/node.rs`). The oracle, opentide 0.23.0, reads it with PyYAML's YAML 1.1 loader. Each row is one document: what the oracle reads (Python's value, or why it refuses the file), what opentide-schema reads, and, where they differ, why. Strings are quoted, floats end in `f`.

## Differences

### anchors

YAML 1.2 lets an anchor be defined again; an alias refers to the latest definition. libyaml refused the file.

Changelog: **Tide objects are read as YAML 1.2**. Changes how an existing workspace file reads: no.

### bom

A byte order mark may start the file; inside a value it refuses the file, as YAML 1.2 says. The oracle kept it in the string.

Changelog: **Tide objects are read as YAML 1.2**. Changes how an existing workspace file reads: **yes** (a question for the maintainers in the PR).

### booleans

YAML 1.2 has two booleans, `true` and `false` (also written `True`, `TRUE`, `False`, `FALSE`). `yes`, `no`, `on`, `off` are strings, which YAML 1.1 read as booleans. A boolean field written `enabled: yes` is now a type error (`bool_type`).

Changelog: **Tide objects are read as YAML 1.2**. Changes how an existing workspace file reads: **yes** (a question for the maintainers in the PR).

### duplicate-keys

A key is the same key when it is the same type and value, as the YAML specification defines node equality: `null` and `~` collide (the oracle compared the raw text and kept the last), and `1`, `1.0` and `"1"` are three keys (the oracle compared Python values or raw text). A repeated key refuses the file, as it did.

Changelog: **Tide objects are read as YAML 1.2**. Changes how an existing workspace file reads: **yes** (a question for the maintainers in the PR).

### empty-key

YAML 1.2 allows an empty implicit key (`: 1` is the key `null`); a model reports it as a key that is not a string. libyaml refused the file.

Changelog: **Tide objects are read as YAML 1.2**. Changes how an existing workspace file reads: no.

### floats

YAML 1.2 reads `1e3` and `1e+3` as floats; YAML 1.1 needs a dot (`1.0e3`) and read them as strings.

Changelog: **Tide objects are read as YAML 1.2**. Changes how an existing workspace file reads: no.

### integer-range

An integer is a 64-bit integer. One that does not fit refuses the file, where saphyr alone would read it as an approximate float or a string; the oracle read Python's unbounded `int`. No Tide field holds such a number.

Changelog: **Tide objects are read as YAML 1.2**. Changes how an existing workspace file reads: no.

### integers

YAML 1.2 integers are decimal, `0o` octal and `0x` hexadecimal. `017` is 17 (YAML 1.1: 15, octal), `0o17` is 15 (YAML 1.1: a string); `0b101`, `1_000` and sexagesimal `1:20` are strings (YAML 1.1: integers).

Changelog: **Tide objects are read as YAML 1.2**. Changes how an existing workspace file reads: **yes** (a question for the maintainers in the PR).

### line-breaks

YAML 1.2 breaks lines on line feed and carriage return only: NEL (U+0085) and the line and paragraph separators (U+2028, U+2029) are characters of the text. YAML 1.1 broke lines on them.

Changelog: **Tide objects are read as YAML 1.2**. Changes how an existing workspace file reads: no.

### merge-keys

Merge keys (`<<: *base`) are a YAML 1.1 type that YAML 1.2 dropped: `<<` is an ordinary key. A model reports it as an unknown key (`extra_forbidden`); the oracle merged the anchored mapping in.

Changelog: **Tide objects are read as YAML 1.2**. Changes how an existing workspace file reads: **yes** (a question for the maintainers in the PR).

### tab-after-colon

saphyr refuses a tab right after a mapping's `:` (`a:<TAB>1`), which libyaml accepts and the YAML 1.2 grammar allows as separating white space. A space before the tab (`a: <TAB>1`) is read by both.

Changelog: **Tide objects are read as YAML 1.2**. Changes how an existing workspace file reads: **yes** (a question for the maintainers in the PR).

### tags

Tags follow the YAML 1.2 core schema: the non-specific `!` makes a string (`! 12` is the string 12), an explicit `!!int`, `!!float`, `!!bool` or `!!null` must fit its text, and other tags (`!!binary`, `!!set`, `!!omap`, `!!pairs`, `!!timestamp`, local tags) refuse the file, where the oracle constructed Python objects. A plain `=` or `<<` is a string (PyYAML had no constructor for them).

Changelog: **Tide objects are read as YAML 1.2**. Changes how an existing workspace file reads: no.

### timestamps

YAML 1.2's core schema has no timestamp type: a date is the string written. The oracle turned a date or timestamp into ISO 8601 text (`2026-01-01 10:00:00` became `2026-01-01T10:00:00`) and refused the file when the date cannot exist (`2026-02-30`). The text is kept as written; checking that a date exists is the date field's own check (UC-1.3), not the YAML reader's.

Changelog: **Tide objects are read as YAML 1.2**. Changes how an existing workspace file reads: **yes** (a question for the maintainers in the PR).

## Cases

### bool

| Case | YAML | Oracle (PyYAML, YAML 1.1) | opentide-schema (saphyr, YAML 1.2) | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bool-words | `"a: yes\nb: Yes\nc: YES\nd: no\ne: No\nf: NO\ng: on\nh: On\ni: ON\nj: off\nk: Off\nl: OFF\nm: true\nn: True\no: TRUE\np: false\nq: False\nr: FALSE\n"` | {"a": true, "b": true, "c": true, "d": false, "e": false, "f": false, "g": true, "h": true, "i": true, "j": false, "k": false, "l": false, "m": true, "n": true, "o": true, "p": false, "q": false, "r": false} | {"a": "yes", "b": "Yes", "c": "YES", "d": "no", "e": "No", "f": "NO", "g": "on", "h": "On", "i": "ON", "j": "off", "k": "Off", "l": "OFF", "m": true, "n": true, "o": true, "p": false, "q": false, "r": false} | [booleans](#booleans) |
| bool-not-words | `"a: y\nb: n\nc: Y\nd: N\ne: yEs\nf: tRUE\ng: oN\nh: 'yes'\ni: \"no\"\nj: !!str on\nk: t\nl: f\n"` | {"a": "y", "b": "n", "c": "Y", "d": "N", "e": "yEs", "f": "tRUE", "g": "oN", "h": "yes", "i": "no", "j": "on", "k": "t", "l": "f"} | {"a": "y", "b": "n", "c": "Y", "d": "N", "e": "yEs", "f": "tRUE", "g": "oN", "h": "yes", "i": "no", "j": "on", "k": "t", "l": "f"} | same |
| bool-keys | `"yes: 1\noff: 2\ny: 3\n"` | {true: 1, false: 2, "y": 3} | {"yes": 1, "off": 2, "y": 3} | [booleans](#booleans) |
| bool-explicit-tag | `"a: !!bool yes\nb: !!bool false\n"` | {"a": true, "b": false} | refused: 'yes' is not a valid value for the tag !!bool (line 1, column 4) | [booleans](#booleans) |

|---|---|---|---|---|
| null-forms | `"a: ~\nb: null\nc: Null\nd: NULL\ne:\nf: nULL\ng: 'null'\nh: \"~\"\ni: !!null ''\n"` | {"a": null, "b": null, "c": null, "d": null, "e": null, "f": "nULL", "g": "null", "h": "~", "i": null} | {"a": null, "b": null, "c": null, "d": null, "e": null, "f": "nULL", "g": "null", "h": "~", "i": null} | same |
| null-in-flow | `"a: [~, null]\nb: {x: , y: ~}\n"` | {"a": [null, null], "b": {"x": null, "y": null}} | {"a": [null, null], "b": {"x": null, "y": null}} | same |
| null-flow-empty-entry | `"a: [~, , ]\n"` | refused: while parsing a flow node | refused: while parsing a node, did not find expected node content (line 1, column 8) | same |
| null-key | `"~: a\nnull: b\n"` | {null: "b"} | refused: the key 'null' is repeated; it is first written on line 1 (line 2, column 1) | [duplicate-keys](#duplicate-keys) |

| date-year-zero | `"a: 0000-01-01\n"` | refused: '0000-01-01' is not a valid date (year 0 is out of range) | {"a": "0000-01-01"} | [timestamps](#timestamps) |
| date-leap-day | `"a: 2024-02-29\nb: 2000-02-29\n"` | {"a": "2024-02-29", "b": "2000-02-29"} | {"a": "2024-02-29", "b": "2000-02-29"} | same |
| date-not-leap | `"a: 1900-02-29\n"` | refused: '1900-02-29' is not a valid date (day is out of range for month) | {"a": "1900-02-29"} | [timestamps](#timestamps) |
| date-key | `"2026-01-01: a\n"` | {"2026-01-01": "a"} | {"2026-01-01": "a"} | same |
